causalModel.founding: The gangs that work the lower channel are hired out of Alten Corimont. The tree that their families answer to stands nine bends upriver. The water there is still fresh enough to drink. The village grew round the tree.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The village stands on a low island of firm ground in a bend of the river. The island lies above the salt. The tree's roots reach the water at a bank.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: A tribe keeps a tree. The tribe hires its own people out downriver. There is no other coin here.
causalModel.pressures: Every year more of the village's adults are on a downriver roll. Fewer of them now stand before the tree each year.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the tree withdraws, the village is left nine bends from the work.

why.what: The kin house is a thatch house with a door. The children and grandparents of the gang workers live there together.
why.whyHere: The households that remain moved into one house when their adults went downriver.
why.whySpot: The kin house stands in the north-west of the ring, on the shore.
why.whyNeighbours: The rest of the ring lies south and east of the kin house, round the tree.
why.playerPurpose: The kin house is kept apart for the children and the old.
why.microGeography: A strip of firm shore lies between the ring and the river.

districts.notes: Five thatch and bamboo houses, an empty frame and a guar awning in a loose ring round the tree on its bank; the hatchery pool and the landing below the bank on the river side.

why.what: The village holds the houses round the tree's foot, the shrine, the hatchery and the landing.
why.whyHere: The tree stands on the highest ground of the island. It stands over the bank where the river bends.
why.whySpot: The firm crown of the island rises one to three metres over the river.
why.whyNeighbours: Marsh and river lie on every side. The nearest neighbours are a day's poling downriver.
why.playerPurpose: The village holds the tree that rules the gang families, its minder, a bed and a trader.
why.microGeography: The village stands on a low island of firm ground in a river bend. The east bank of the island falls to the water under the tree.

districts.notes: The bamboo pieces among the thatch: the trade house built the downriver way, the guar awning and the half-stripped frame.

why.what: The downriver houses are the village's bamboo buildings. The trade house is built in the style of the lower channel.
why.whyHere: Households that came back from the gangs built the way that the downriver camps build.
why.whySpot: The bamboo buildings stand among the thatch houses of the ring. They stand on the same island.
why.whyNeighbours: The thatch houses of the ring stand between the downriver houses.
why.playerPurpose: The downriver houses hold the trader, the pond guar and the empty frame.
why.microGeography: The district stands on the same low island. The island lies one to three metres over the river.

districts.notes: Eight houses west of the main road, on one lane with a step to each door.

why.what: The road houses hold households of a smith, cutters, net menders, a boat builder and a dyer.
why.whyHere: The ring round the tree is full. Younger households built on the firm ground past the road.
why.whySpot: The district lies west of the road. The island stays dry and level there.
why.whyNeighbours: The road runs to the east of the district. The ring houses and the tree stand beyond the road.
why.playerPurpose: The trades of the village are done in these houses. A traveller on the road passes these houses first.
why.microGeography: The ground is flat and dry, west of the road. It stands a few metres over the marsh.

districts.notes: The two thatch houses at the ends of the west lane, the smith's and the boat builder's.

why.what: The thatch ends hold two thatch houses on posts. These houses are built like the ring houses. The bamboo huts around them are built differently.
why.whyHere: The smith and the boat builder came out from the ring. They built as their parents had.
why.whySpot: The houses stand at the west end of the lane and on its north side. They are nearest the marsh and the river.
why.whyNeighbours: The bamboo huts of the west lane stand between the two thatch houses.
why.playerPurpose: The two houses show the ring's way of building. The ring's own families carried that way of building out past the road.
why.microGeography: The ground is firm at the edges of the west quarter. It stands a few metres over the marsh.

parcels.orientationWhy: The minder's house door faces south across the common to the trunk.

why.what: The minder's house is the tree-minder's thatch house. It is the nearest house to the tree.
why.whyHere: The tree-minder is called to the tree at any hour. The minder sleeps within sight of the tree.
why.whySpot: The house stands on flat ground north of the tree. The ground lies above the north shore.
why.whyNeighbours: The tree lies south of the minder's house. The empty frame and the kin house are to the north-west.
why.playerPurpose: The tree-minder lives in this house. The minder says plainly what the tree's silence means.
why.microGeography: The house stands on firm low ground about a metre over the river.

playerPurpose.note: The tree-minder says plainly what it means when the tree goes quiet.

parcels.orientationWhy: The elder's house door faces east across the common to the shrine at the tree's foot.

why.what: The elder's house is a thatch house. The elder gives a bed to a stranger who brings news.
why.whyHere: The elder looks after the village's guests. The elder also keeps the village's account of who has gone downriver.
why.whySpot: The house stands in the middle of the island, west of the tree.
why.whyNeighbours: The trade house stands south of the elder's house, beside the path from the landing. The kin house stands north of it.
why.playerPurpose: A stranger is given a bed for the night in this house.
why.microGeography: The house stands on the flat crown of the island. The crown is two metres over the river.

playerPurpose.note: A bed for a stranger who brings news from downriver.
The elder keeps count of who has gone down to the gangs.
MQ01: the elder gives the stranger who brought the news a place to rest.

parcels.orientationWhy: The trade house door faces east onto the path from the landing.

why.what: The trade house is a bamboo house built the downriver way. Trade with the boats is done here.
why.whyHere: One household came back from the gangs with coin. It built in the style of the lower channel.
why.whySpot: The trade house is the first house on the way in from the west.
why.whyNeighbours: The elder's house is north of the trade house. The fishers' house is to the south-east.
why.playerPurpose: The trade house belongs to the village's trader. The trader gives cut cane, cord and smoked fish for what the boats bring.
why.microGeography: The house stands on the west side of the island. The track comes up from the marsh there.

playerPurpose.note: Cut cane, cord and smoked fish, traded for what the boats bring upriver.

parcels.orientationWhy: The kin house door faces south-east, towards the tree. Every household answers to the tree.

why.what: The kin house is a bamboo hut. Children and grandparents share it. Their adults are all downriver.
why.whyHere: The households that remain have moved in together.
why.whySpot: The hut stands in the north-west of the island, on the ring round the tree.
why.whyNeighbours: The elder's house is south of the kin house. The minder's house is across the common to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The families of the gang workers live here while their adults are away.
why.microGeography: The hut stands on low firm ground on the north-west shore.

playerPurpose.note: The grandparents keep count of which gang hired each of their adults.
The children repeat what the boats say about the work downriver.

parcels.orientationWhy: The fishers' house door faces north-east, towards the tree and the ring path.

why.what: The fishers' house is a thatch house by the south shore.
why.whyHere: The household that still fishes lives nearest the water that it fishes.
why.whySpot: The house stands in the south of the island, above the shore.
why.whyNeighbours: The trade house is west of the fishers' house. The hatchery and the landing are east of it.
why.playerPurpose: The fishing household keeps nets and a drying rack by the shore.
why.microGeography: The house stands on the gentle south slope down to the river.

playerPurpose.note: The fishers watch every boat that comes round the bend.

parcels.orientationWhy: The empty frame's open side faces south, towards the tree. It was built to face the tree.

why.what: The empty frame is the frame of a house half taken down. Its thatch is gone.
why.whyHere: The family that built it went downriver on a roll. The family did not come back for it.
why.whySpot: The frame stands at the far north edge of the village, last on the ring.
why.whyNeighbours: The minder's house and the kin house are south of the frame.
why.playerPurpose: Few people are left in the village. The frame has room for more families than the village has.
why.microGeography: The frame stands on low ground at the north shore, just above the water.

parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/orcawninghalf01

parcels.orientationWhy: The guar shelter's open side faces south-west to the tree.

why.what: The guar shelter is an open awning. The pond guar are kept under it.
why.whyHere: The guar are kept for the warmth that they give the hatchery.
why.whySpot: The shelter stands on the bank top beside the path down to the landing.
why.whyNeighbours: The tree is south-west of the shelter. The landing and the hatchery are below it to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The pond guar are kept here out of the rain.
why.microGeography: The shelter stands on the lip of the east bank, over the river.

parcels.assetRef: htbm:here there be monsters - curse of cipactli/architecture/villages/argonian/orcawning01

parcels.orientationWhy: The totems face west, towards the path from the landing.

why.what: The shrine stands at the tree's foot. The shrine holds two totems, offerings and candles. The hatchery pool lies below the bank. Fired-clay lids cover the clutches beside the pool.
why.whyHere: The village exists because of the tree.
why.whySpot: The shrine stands at the west foot of the trunk. The way in reaches the tree there.
why.whyNeighbours: The trunk rises behind the shrine. The houses ring the common in front of it.
why.playerPurpose: The tree-minder tends the offerings at the shrine.
why.microGeography: The shrine stands on flat ground at the foot of the trunk.

playerPurpose.note: MQ01: the tree withdraws here at its foot.
MQ01: the player finds where the harvest was cut.
MQ01: the hatchery pool under the roots.
MQ01: the foot of the tree, where the minder waits.

parcels.orientationWhy: The dock runs east from the shore into the river.

why.what: The landing is a stage where the boats from downriver tie up.
why.whyHere: The village is reached by water as much as by the track.
why.whySpot: The landing lies on the gentle north-east shore, below the guar shelter.
why.whyNeighbours: The hatchery is south of the landing, at the foot of the bank.
why.playerPurpose: A boat from downriver lands here. A traveller can arrive here by water.
why.microGeography: The landing stands on a shallow shelf of the river off a low shore.

parcels.orientationWhy: The smith's house door faces the step that turns off the lane to the north-west corner.

why.what: The smith's house is a thatch house. The village smith lives there. The smith mends iron from the boats.
why.whyHere: Hooks, blades and nails come upriver broken. The smith mends them.
why.whySpot: The house stands at the far west end of the lane. It is away from the thatch of the ring.
why.whyNeighbours: The cane cutters live just south of the smith, across the lane.
why.playerPurpose: The household is at work. The smith's tools and the iron waiting for mending are there.
why.microGeography: The house stands on the last dry ground before the marsh to the west.

playerPurpose.note: The smith's forge, kept hot for hooks and blades off the boats.

parcels.orientationWhy: The reed cutters' house door faces north onto the lane to the road.

why.what: The reed cutters' house is a bamboo house. The family cuts reed for thatch and mats.
why.whyHere: Every roof in the village needs new reed each wet season.
why.whySpot: The house stands on the lane, close to the reed beds. The reed beds lie at the west edge of the island.
why.whyNeighbours: The cane cutters are to the west. The net menders are across the lane to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The family lives in the house on the walk through the quarter.
why.microGeography: The house stands on level ground just south of the lane. It is clear of the bank.

playerPurpose.note: The cutters work the reed beds at dawn and see the boats that pass at night.

parcels.orientationWhy: The net menders' house door faces the short step from the lane.

why.what: The net menders' house is a bamboo house. The old net menders work there through the dry months.
why.whyHere: The fishers' nets tear on snags in the river. The nets are brought here for mending.
why.whySpot: The house stands north of the lane, halfway between the road and the ring.
why.whyNeighbours: The boat builder lives to the north-east. The reed cutters live across the lane.
why.playerPurpose: The household's work ties it to the fishers by the river.
why.microGeography: The house stands on firm ground north of the lane, above the wet hollow.

playerPurpose.note: The menders know whose nets came back torn. They also know where each was set.

parcels.orientationWhy: The boat builder's house door faces west onto the end of its step.

why.what: The boat builder's house is a thatch house. The family builds and patches the village's boats.
why.whyHere: The village lives by the river. Every boat needs patching after the wet.
why.whySpot: The house stands on the north side of the quarter, on the way down to the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The net menders live to the south-west, a short walk off.
why.playerPurpose: The village builds its own boats. This house is the sign of it.
why.microGeography: The house stands on firm ground on the north side, towards the river.

playerPurpose.note: The boat builder's bench, with pitch and cane for patching a hull.

parcels.orientationWhy: The cane cutters' house door faces the west end of the lane.

why.what: The cane cutters' house is a bamboo house. The cane cutters supply the trade house.
why.whyHere: Cut cane is what the village trades to the boats.
why.whySpot: The house stands at the west end of the lane, near the cane at the island's edge.
why.whyNeighbours: The smith lives to the north. The reed cutters live to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The household cuts the cane sold at the trade house.
why.microGeography: The house stands on level ground at the west end of the lane.

playerPurpose.note: The cutters count every bundle that goes to the trade house. The cutters know the fee that each boat is charged.

parcels.orientationWhy: The dyer's house door faces the end of the dyer's path.

why.what: The dyer's house is a bamboo house. Cloth and cord are dyed there with marsh roots.
why.whyHere: Dye stinks. The dyer works at the far south-west of the quarter.
why.whySpot: The house stands in the south-west corner, at the end of its own path.
why.whyNeighbours: The hunter lives to the east, along the south lane.
why.playerPurpose: The house stands at the end of a side path. It is worth the walk to find.
why.microGeography: The hut stands on the south-west edge of the dry ground. The ground there is graded level for the hut.

playerPurpose.note: Dyed cloth and cord, with the marsh roots that give the colour.

routes.why: The way in starts at the track on the west shore. It passes the trade house to the shrine. It then runs on round the tree to the landing.
A path runs from the shrine north between the houses. It ends at the empty frame.
A step leads from the north path to the elder's door.
A step leads from the north path to the minder's door.
A step leads from the north path to the kin house door.
A step leads from the way in to the trade house door.
A step leads from the way in down to the fishers' door.
The last steps lead from the way in to the shrine totems.
A step leads from the way to the guar awning.
A path runs along the foot of the bank. It links the landing to the hatchery lids.
A lane runs west from the main road through the road houses.
A step leads from the lane to the net menders' door.
A step leads from the lane to the reed cutters' door.
A step leads from the end of the lane to the cane cutters' door.
A path runs from the lane north and west. It ends at the smith's door.
A path runs from the lane north to the boat builders' door.
A path runs from the lane south to the hunter's door.
A side path leaves the south path. It ends at the dyer's door.
The heartland footpath carries on east from the edge of the village. It joins the lane through the road houses.
A short walk leads from the road houses up to the ring. A traveller who stops at the road can find the tree.

landmarks.notes: One broad low Hist on the bank top, its root running down into the hatchery pool.

why.what: The landmark is the village's Hist tree. The tree rules the gang families of the lower channel.
why.whyHere: The villagers built the village round the tree. They built it sixty years ago and more.
why.whySpot: The tree stands on the highest ground of the island. It stands on the bank over the river.
why.whyNeighbours: The houses ring the foot of the tree. The hatchery and the landing lie below it on the river side.
why.playerPurpose: The tree's withdrawal starts the main quest.
why.microGeography: The tree stands on the crown of the bank. The crown is three metres over the river.

questSockets.why: The socket is the cut in the trunk above the root that runs to the pool. The harvest attempt severed the tree from its eggs there.
The socket is the hatchery pool at the toe of the bank. It lies beside the clay lids.
The socket is the shrine at the west foot of the trunk.
The socket is the elder's door. The elder gives a stranger a bed for the night there.
The socket is the common in front of the shrine. The village gathers there when the chimes stop.

occupants.cultureRole: Net mender who works for the fishers
Dyer who colours the cut reed
Smith who mends the village's tools

approaches.sequence: The track comes up out of the marsh onto the west end of the island. The broad crown of the tree shows over the reeds first. The trade house beside the way comes next. The shrine at the foot of the trunk follows.
approaches.wayfinding: The way runs straight from the track to the shrine. The houses stand round the tree.

approaches.sequence: From the river the chimes carry before the bend. Round the bend the tree stands on its bank. The hatchery pool lies under the tree. The landing stage lies beside the pool.
approaches.wayfinding: The landing runs out from the low shore north of the hatchery.

approaches.sequence: The heartland track comes in from the west. The reed-cutters' bamboo hut is the first roof in sight.
approaches.wayfinding: The traveller keeps to the track. The dyer's path leaves the track at the edge of the huts.

networkTerminals.why: The village's own track comes up from the marsh at the west end of the island. The way in starts there.
The heartland track is a footpath by the time it reaches the village from the west. It carries on east between the first huts. It joins the lane through the road houses.

combatSpaces.why: The open common lies between the houses and the shrine. The common is level and clear.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The lore source is the catalogue record Nine Bends (hist-village, M2). The record describes a tribe, its tree-minder and the households whose adults are downriver.
scaleGrounding.why: The minder and ten households live in the houses round the tree and west of the road. One house stands empty. Another house is half taken down. So many adults work downriver.

candidates.why: The chosen site is the low island in the bend. The tree stands on the bank top over the deep water. Firm ground west of the tree holds a ring of houses.
The plotted anchor lies on the east lip of the island over the river.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The plotted anchor sits on the steep east bank. The bank has no room for the tree and a ring of houses. The bank drops two metres to the water in four.
